summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, style, or format consistently, or teach it a narrow domain skill that prompting and RAG cannot reliably deliver. RAG is the right choice when you need up-to-date or proprietary knowledge retrieval, and prompt engineering is best for quick behavioral steering without infrastructure. In practice, teams often combine fine-tuning for form/behavior with RAG for facts.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output format, tone, or structured responses that prompting alone cannot guarantee reliably at scale.
Fine-tune when you have a specialized domain (legal, medical, code) with ample high-quality labeled examples that the base model handles poorly.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the core need is injecting current, frequently-changing, or proprietary knowledge rather than altering model behavior.
Fine-tune to reduce latency and cost by shrinking long few-shot prompts into learned behavior, or to distill a larger model into a smaller faster one.
